descriptions.AU4.1: Login `Set-Cookie` parsed: name `__Host-mfx_sid`; value matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$` and decodes to 32 bytes; attribute set exactly `{Path=/, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Max-Age=2592000}`; no `Domain`, no `Expires` conflict. 200 logins → 200 unique values.
descriptions.AU4.2: `/api/auth/csrf` with no pre cookie → `Set-Cookie: __Host-mfx_pre=…` attributes exactly `{Path=/, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Max-Age=1800}`; with a valid pre cookie → no new `Set-Cookie`; body key set exactly `["csrf"]`, `Cache-Control: no-store`.
descriptions.AU5.1: (Q13) KV key equals exactly `"sess:" + lowercase-hex sha256(rawId)` (64 chars, `^sess:[0-9a-f]{64}$`); no KV key or value contains the raw id.
descriptions.AU5.2: (G1, R7) Token storage is only the `SESSION` DO: after login, the DO instance `sess:<hex>`'s storage holds an R7 `v1.<kid>.<iv>.<ct>` value whose bytes contain none of `ACCESS1`/`REFRESH1` (raw, base64, hex); with `SESSION_ENC_KEY` swapped for another key, the same cookie → comment POST 401 `signed_out`, never 500.
descriptions.AU5.3: (G10, 1.4.11) the `sess:*` put after login has `expirationTtl === 60` and no `expiration` option; and after the same write the `SESSION` DO's `storage.getAlarm()` equals `min(last_seen+30d, created+90d)` exactly (ms).
descriptions.AU5.4: (R15, G10) Rolling is held by the `SESSION` DO, not KV: a user-acting request and `/me` at `last_seen+23h` → `/me` is `{signed_in:true,…}` (KV entry long expired, rebuilt from the DO per G10: exactly 1 `sess:*` put, `expirationTtl === 60`, value's `last_seen` unchanged), DO `last_seen` and alarm unchanged, no `Set-Cookie`; at `+25h` → DO `last_seen` updated, alarm moved to `min(last_seen+30d, created+90d)`, `Set-Cookie` `Max-Age=2592000`, and the KV put still `expirationTtl === 60`; 10 `/me` calls within 24 h → 0 `Set-Cookie`.
descriptions.AU5.6: (R15, §0c G6 as ruled inclusive in 1.4.8 by Web Lead: a session expires when `now - created >= 90d`) Absolute cap 90 days from `created`, with daily use so the rolling TTL never lapses: at `created+89d` → valid (comment POST 2xx); at `created+90d−1s` → valid; at exactly `created+90d` → signed out (comment POST 401 `signed_out`, cookie cleared, DO state and KV entry deleted, 0 BSI) (Q1, decided by G6), and the DO's `storage.list()` is empty and `getAlarm()` is null; at `created+91d` → signed out. A refresh at 89d doesn't move `created` (still signed out at 90d).
descriptions.ENC.T2: Entry written with `kid` of `SESSION_ENC_KEY_PREV`; after rotation the session reads fine; the next write uses the current `kid`; nothing is ever encrypted with PREV (spy on `encrypt` key handles).
descriptions.ENC.T3: (R7 AAD = `SESSION` instance name, 1.4.9) Ciphertext copied from instance `sess:A`'s DO storage into `sess:B`'s (real DO under Miniflare, named direct DO-storage seed) → B treated as absent: comment POST and leaderboard 401 `signed_out`, 0 BSI, HTTP status never 500. **Control (vacuity):** the same bytes written back into `sess:A` → A's comment POST succeeds with `Bearer ACCESS1` (proves the copy was a valid ciphertext and only the AAD differs). `/me` is KV-only (R5) and is not the assertion.
descriptions.ENC.T4: Ciphertext produced under an unrelated 32-byte key → absent, never 500. `importKey` called once per isolate across 20 requests.
descriptions.AU5.5: (named direct DO-storage seed) Flip one byte of the stored ciphertext / IV in the `SESSION` DO → next comment POST 401 `signed_out`, 0 BSI.
descriptions.AU5.x: (1.4.7 §5a, R7; re-checked against the 1.4.9 DO storage model: KV is the token-free `/me` cache, so the scan is unchanged and still applies to every KV write incl. after alarm and logout) KV never holds token material. A recording KV fake (`AUTH_SESSIONS`) logs every `put(key, value, options)` (incl. `expirationTtl`, `expiration` and every `metadata` field), every `delete`, and every `get`/`list`, and keeps the final state. Drive the real routes through: (a) password login; (b) a user-acting call that triggers refresh with BSI rotating the pair (`ACCESS2`/`REFRESH2`); (c) a Google callback; (d) logout; (e) session expiry (90-day cap and refresh failure 401). Then enumerate every recorded put (key, value, every option incl. metadata) **and** every final KV entry via `list()`/`get(..., {type:"text"})`, and assert none contains: `ACCESS1`, `REFRESH1`, `ACCESS2`, `REFRESH2` in raw, standard base64, base64url (padded and unpadded), URL-encoded (`encodeURIComponent`) and JSON-escaped (`JSON.stringify(x).slice(1,-1)`) forms; any substring matching `/(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])v1\./` (R7 ciphertext prefix); and, for every value or metadata that parses as JSON, any key at any depth matching `/token|refresh|access/i`. **Vacuity check (same test):** before the flows, the test does one known benign `env.AUTH_SESSIONS.put("qa:probe", "benign", {metadata:{probe:1}, expirationTtl:60})` through the same fake and asserts the recorder saw it with all three arguments; it also asserts ≥1 `sess:*` put was recorded during (a) (the `/me` cache write), so an empty recorder fails the test instead of passing it.
descriptions.AU5.y: (1.4.9, CQ; real `SESSION` DO class under Miniflare, fake clock) Storage and alarm lifecycle, each its own case with a session created by real login: (a) logout; (b) refresh failure (`/oauth/token` `invalid_grant` 400 and 401; 1.34); (c) 30 days idle — advance the clock to `last_seen+30d` and run the alarm (`runDurableObjectAlarm`); (d) the 90-day cap (age >= 90d, daily use). After each: the DO's `storage.list()` returns an empty Map **and** `storage.getAlarm()` is null; at (c) also `last_seen+30d−1s` → storage still present (alarm not early). Normal writes: after login, after a refresh (AU7.1), and after the >24 h rewrite (AU5.4) there is exactly one alarm, at exactly `min(last_seen+30d, created+90d)` — checked with `created` such that each operand is the min once (e.g. `created` at day 0, `last_seen` at day 65 → alarm at day 90; `last_seen` at day 10 → day 40). Writes are counted with a spy on `setAlarm`: exactly one `setAlarm` per storage write. **Vacuity:** before (a)–(d), `storage.list()` is non-empty and holds an R7 `v1.` value.
descriptions.AU5.k: (§0d B3, S-G16: the `SESSION` DO is the source of truth for writes) Login; advance the fake clock to +61 s. **Control (KV entry really gone):** the recording KV fake's `get("sess:<hex>")` returns `null` and its TTL bookkeeping shows the entry expired at +60 s. Then comment POST (`H_OK`) → **201** and leaderboard GET → **200**, both resolved via the DO (1 DO call each), with **0** KV `get`/`list` calls recorded during those two requests and exactly the expected BSI calls (no refresh). Vacuity: the same two requests at +1 s also succeed (proves the routes work) and the recorder logged ≥1 KV op during login.
descriptions.AU5.z: (1.4.11 §0c G10) KV `/me` TTL is always 60 s. Recording KV fake (as AU5.x: every `put(key, value, options)`, honouring `expirationTtl` on the fake clock) over the real routes, each flow its own case: (a) password login; (b) `/me` hit (within 60 s of a put) → 0 puts in this flow is **expected** for (b) only, and the response is served from KV (0 DO calls); (c) `/me` miss at put+61 s → rebuilt from the `SESSION` DO: exactly 1 put, body `{signed_in:true, public_name}` equal to before the miss, 1 DO read, 0 BSI; (d) the >24 h rewrite (AU5.4); (e) a user-acting call triggering a refresh, two cases: rotating (`ACCESS2/REFRESH2`) and non-rotating (`ACCESS2`, same `REFRESH1`; 1.22, CQ N7), each with ≥1 `sess:*` put; (f) the Google callback; (g) the 90-day boundary: at `created+90d−1s` a `/me` miss rebuilds with TTL 60, at `created+90d` the DO is empty → `/me` `{signed_in:false}` and **no** `sess:*` put. Assertion: every `put` to a `sess:*` key in every flow has `options.expirationTtl === 60` exactly (number), no `expiration` key, and no put without options. **Vacuity:** ≥1 `sess:*` put recorded in each of (a), (c), (d), (e), (f) and (g)'s 90d−1s step (each counted separately; (b) is the hit control and must show 0 puts). (h) **DO-down miss** (G10 as ruled in 1.4.12 → S-G18): `SESSION` unbound / throwing / >1 s (each its own case), `/me` at put+61 s → exactly **503**, body exactly `{"error":"unavailable"}`, `Retry-After: 300`; 0 BSI calls; 0 KV puts (any key); **no** `Set-Cookie` clearing or replacing `__Host-mfx_sid` (cookie kept); after the outage ends the same cookie's `/me` → `{signed_in:true,…}` rebuilt with TTL 60 (proves the session survived). Client mount: on that 503 the UI renders the signed-out state, makes 0 logout calls and 0 requests that would clear the cookie.
descriptions.AU6.1: Fixation: request login with `Cookie: __Host-mfx_sid=attackerChosenValueAAAA…` → new sid ≠ it; no KV key for `h(attackerChosen)`; afterwards the attacker value → comment POST 401 NW (A-T1).
descriptions.AU6.2: (R4) A silent refresh keeps the sid: no `Set-Cookie: __Host-mfx_sid`, the same `sess:<h(sid)>` key is rewritten (1 put, 0 delete), and the next comment POST with the same cookie succeeds with `Bearer ACCESS2`.
descriptions.AU6.3: Google callback with a pre-existing sid → the old `SESSION` DO instance is cleared and its KV `/me` entry deleted; a new sid and a new DO instance are issued.
descriptions.AU7.1: `access_exp − now = 59 s` → comment POST makes exactly 1 `/oauth/token` call (1.34: BSI-C3 retired), form body `toStrictEqual({grant_type:"refresh_token",refresh_token:REFRESH1,client_id:CID,client_secret:SECRET_CANARY})` per AU27.1, 0 proxy requests, then the BSI write carries `Bearer ACCESS2`; the `SESSION` DO storage now decrypts to `ACCESS2/REFRESH2` and the KV `/me` entry holds no token (AU5.x). At 61 s → 0 `/oauth/token` and 0 proxy calls.
descriptions.AU7.2: (Q15) BSI 401 on the user call → call, 1 refresh, 1 retry (exactly 3 BSI calls); a second 401 → 401 `{"error":"signed_out"}`, `SESSION` DO storage empty with no alarm (`deleteAll()` + `deleteAlarm()`), KV `/me` entry deleted, cookie cleared, no 4th call (S-G16, §5.2 S4).
descriptions.AU7.3: Refresh 400 and 401 → `SESSION` DO storage empty and no alarm, KV `/me` entry deleted, response 401 `{"error":"signed_out"}`, `Set-Cookie` clears sid.
descriptions.AU7.4: (G1) Two concurrent near-expiry user-acting calls for one session in one isolate → exactly 1 `/oauth/token` call (1.34), 0 proxy requests,, made from inside the `SESSION` DO (spy on the DO's fetch, 0 refresh calls from the Worker module).
descriptions.AU7.6: (re-added 1.22 per CQ B1; §0c G1; refresh serialisation, no rotation premise) Runs against the **real `SESSION` DO class under Miniflare or `unstable_dev`** (a hand-written stand-in fails the item). KV fake stale (previous value for 60 s after each `put`, per isolate). Two isolates make concurrent user-acting calls (comment POST, leaderboard GET) for one session, both needing refresh. **Variant N (non-rotating, required):** `/oauth/token` (`grant_type=refresh_token`) mock returns `ACCESS2` with the same `REFRESH1`. **Variant N0 (spec 1.6.4 "or none"):** mock returns `ACCESS2` and no `refresh_token`; the DO keeps `REFRESH1`. **Variant R (QA, stores-what-BSI-returns):** mock returns `ACCESS2/REFRESH2`, `REFRESH1` again → 400 `invalid_grant`. Each variant: exactly **1** upstream `/oauth/token` call; both user calls go out with `Bearer ACCESS2` (neither uses `ACCESS1` nor triggers a second refresh); both 2xx; afterwards `/me` signed in and the DO holds `ACCESS2` and the refresh token BSI returned (N and N0: `REFRESH1`; R: `REFRESH2`). 50 repeats per variant, randomised skew 0–20 ms; 0 failures. (1.31: target `/oauth/token` per spec 1.6.8 §0u.7.) **(1.32, spec 1.6.9 §0v.5) Rotating mock required:** R0 accepted once (→ `ACCESS2`/R1), then R0 → `invalid_grant`; 50 concurrent user-acting calls across the two isolates → exactly 1 `/oauth/token` call, every caller succeeds with `ACCESS2`, the DO holds R1, the user stays signed in. Variant N0 (no `refresh_token` → keep R0) is superseded: that response is now 503 with the pair kept (AU27.7 (d)). **(1.34, spec 1.6.12 §0w.1) Google variant G (required):** the same rotating-mock run with the session created by the Google callback (AU27.10 (a)) instead of password login gives exactly 1 `/oauth/token` call (`grant_type=refresh_token`, metfix.org client), every caller succeeds with `ACCESS2`, and the DO holds R1. 50 repeats, 0 failures.
descriptions.AU7.8: (S-G18, §0c G1, §0c G9 1.4.8) `SESSION` unbound, its DO call throwing, or not answering within 1 s (fake timers); each of the three outage forms is its own case. (i) **User-acting calls:** comment POST and leaderboard GET → 503 `{"error":"unavailable"}`, `Retry-After: 300`, 0 siteverify, 0 BSI; no token read from KV, no anonymous fallback for writes; `/me` for a session that has **not** logged out still answers from its cache while the entry is live (within 60 s of the last put, a KV hit, 0 DO calls); a `/me` **miss** during the outage fails closed (AU5.z row (h)). (ii) **Logout during the outage (G9):** with a valid session (cookie, pre + CSRF), `POST /api/auth/logout` → **204**, empty body; `Set-Cookie` exactly `__Host-mfx_sid=` with `Max-Age=0; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` (same attribute assertion as AU8.1); the KV `sess:*` entry is deleted (recording KV fake shows the `delete` and the final `get` returns null); 0 BSI-C4 calls (no token is reachable: the DO is down and KV holds none, so a BSI call would prove a KV/other token source, see M42h) and 0 KV reads of any non-`sess:` key. Exactly one revoke-failure log line is emitted (captured `console.*`, matched by the PR's documented revoke-failure marker; **vacuity:** the test fails if that line is absent, so the scan below can't pass on silence). Every captured console line from the logout request (args JSON-serialised, incl. descriptions.AU26.10: (QA ID; 1.31 retarget from BSI-C10 to `/oauth/token` 429/5xx and `/me` non-200) Worker clamp of the upstream `Retry-After`: `1` → 1; `0` → 1 (1.23; was 60); `0000017` → 17, `0000000` → 1 (1.25); `600` → 600; `601` → 600; `99999` → 600; `999999` → 600; `1000000` → 600; a 30-digit integer (`123456789012345678901234567890`, beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`) → 600; a 400-digit integer (parses to `Infinity` via `Number`) → 600 (1.23, Web Lead ruling 2026-10-20); missing, `""`, `-5`, `abc`, `1.5`, `1e30`, `17abc` → 60; HTTP-date (`Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT`) → 60 (confirmed by Web Lead 2026-10-20; spec 1.6.3 §0s.12 also names HTTP-date → 60). Output always matches `^[1-9][0-9]*$` and ≤ 600.
descriptions.AU26.11: (QA, CQ N2; spec 1.6.4 §0s.13 (5) `parseRetryAfter`, as superseded by 1.6.5 §0s.14 (2)) One shared parser for login (1.31: `/oauth/token` and `/me` branches; AU27.3/AU26.10) and every comment write/like route (CW13.1): `rg` finds exactly one `parseRetryAfter` definition in `worker/**` (excl. tests) and every BSI-429 branch on login, POST, PATCH, DELETE and like calls it (spy: 1 call per 429). Table, each run through login and all four comment routes with identical output: `17`→17, `017`→17, `0`→1, `000`→1 (1.23; were 60), `0000017`→17, `0000000`→1 (1.25), `600`→600, `601`→600, `99999`→600, `999999`→600, `1000000`→600, 30-digit integer→600, 400-digit integer→600 (1.23, Web Lead ruling 2026-10-20); `1e30`, `+17`, `0x11`, `1.5`, `17abc`, `-5`, `""`, missing, HTTP-date → 60. **Type (1.23):** `parseRetryAfter`'s return type is a branded or literal-constrained 1..600 type; a `*.test-d.ts` checked by `tsc --noEmit` asserts `expectTypeOf(parseRetryAfter("1")).not.toEqualTypeOf<number>()` and holds `// @ts-expect-error` lines assigning `0` and `601` (and a plain `number`) to that type; tsc must fail if the function returns plain `number` (an unused `@ts-expect-error` is an error). Vacuity: the type-check step runs in CI and lists the `.test-d.ts` file. (Leading/trailing spaces are stripped by `Headers` before the Worker sees them, so they are not asserted.)

descriptions.CW12.2: (spec §0r.1, §0r.8, §0r.4) `/me` `moderator` equals `can_moderate` stored in the `SESSION` DO at login (password or Google code exchange) and token refresh (true and false cases); non-boolean `can_moderate` (`"true"`, `1`, absent) → `false`; request header `X-Moderator: 1` / cookie `mfx_mod=1` doesn't change it; `/me` on a KV hit and on a KV miss → **0 BSI calls** (a miss rebuilds from the `SESSION` DO). **CM6-fallback row (§0r.4, 1.5.4 wording):** BSI-C10/C3 responses omit `can_moderate` entirely (BSI-CM6 not shipped) → `/me` `moderator:false` on every login, refresh, KV hit and KV miss; the client shows no moderator controls on others' comments; owner controls (`own:true`) and BSI authorization unchanged. No separate fallback flag exists or is tested. **Moderator-definition row (spec 1.5.2 §0q.1, reworded for 1.5.3 `can_moderate`; QA):** BSI user who is a WordPress administrator (or Daily Fix admin) with `can_moderate:false` → `/me` `moderator:false`; BSI user with role `editor` and `can_moderate:true` → `moderator:true`; the Worker never derives moderator status from a role field in the BSI payload (no role-name logic in `worker/`).
descriptions.CW12.3: (Web Lead addition for 1.19; spec §0r.1, §0r.3) Refresh flip. Start: session whose `SESSION` DO holds `can_moderate:true` and a warm KV `/me` entry with `moderator:true`. A token refresh (user-acting call at `access_exp − now = 59 s`) returns (1.34: `/oauth/token` 200 then) `/me` `can_moderate:false`. Asserts: the refresh rewrites **both** the `SESSION` DO (`can_moderate:false`, alongside the new token pair) and the KV `/me` entry (`moderator:false`, TTL 60); the next `/me` on a KV hit → `moderator:false` (0 BSI calls); after a KV purge (fake clock +61 s or explicit delete), the next `/me` rebuilt from the DO → `moderator:false` (0 BSI calls). The A-T31 stale-display residual (controls visible only until the next refresh) depends on this row.
descriptions.CW13.1: (1.22: Worker clamp per spec 1.6.3) BSI 429 on POST, PATCH, DELETE and like, each case on each of the four routes → 429 `{"error":"rate_limited"}` with exactly: `Retry-After: 17` → `17`; `600` → `600`; `99999` → `600`; `999999` → `600`; `1000000` → `600`; 30-digit integer → `600`; 400-digit integer → `600`; `0` → `1` (1.23, Web Lead ruling 2026-10-20; `0` was 60); `0000017` → `17`, `0000000` → `1` (1.25); `1.5` → `60`; `1e30` → `60`; HTTP-date `Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT` → `60`; `abc` / missing → `60`; exactly 1 BSI call, 0 retries, 0 `cache.delete`. Anonymous GET keeps W6 (429 → 503).
descriptions.CW13.2: (spec §0r.2, §0r.8) Client: 429 `Retry-After: 17` on post, reply, edit, delete and like → rollback; 0 requests for that action for 17 s (fake timers); re-enabled at 17 s.
descriptions.CW14.1: Client: no reply control on any reply row (top-level rows have one). Worker: BSI nested-reply refusal → 400 `{"error":"invalid_parent"}`, 1 BSI call, 0 retries.
descriptions.CW14.2: Client: no like control on `deleted != 0` rows (incl. `[Anonymous]`). Worker: BSI like refusal on a deleted comment → 409 `{"error":"comment_deleted"}`, 0 `cache.delete`.
descriptions.CW15.1: Upstream like body exactly `{"liked":true}` / `{"liked":false}`; client body with `liked` missing, `"true"`, `1`, `null` → 400, 0 BSI; 0 comment reads before the set; every client like request carries boolean `liked`.
descriptions.CW13.3: (spec §0r.2, §0r.8) Client Retry-After cap: 429 `Retry-After: 99999` → control disabled for exactly 600 s, 0 requests, re-enabled at 600 s; remaining time is shown and decreases with the fake clock (`Retry-After: 17` shows 17, then 16 after 1 s).
descriptions.CW16.1: (spec §0r.5, §0r.8) No edit on deleted. Worker: owner and moderator PATCH on a deleted comment, BSI refusal → 409 `{"error":"comment_deleted"}` (fixed body), 1 BSI call, 0 retries, 0 purges (0 `cache.delete`). Client: no edit control on `deleted != 0` rows, incl. for `/me` `moderator:true` and `own:true`.
descriptions.CW16.2: (spec §0r.5, §0r.8; 1.5.4 wording) Idempotent delete. Worker: DELETE of an already-deleted comment, BSI 204 → Worker 204, 1 BSI call, 0 retries; a second DELETE also → 204. **Client 204 rows (1.5.4):** (a) a repeat-delete 204 is handled exactly like a 200 `{deleted:true}` (same rendered row state, same control state, no error message); (b) a 204 clears no cache (0 client comment-cache purges/invalidations; the next read of that date is served as after a 200 `{deleted:true}` without a cache purge).
descriptions.CW16.3: (QA, Web Lead ruling 2026-10-21; rev 1.25) Delete then fresh list. Client test with a recording `fetch` and a stale cached list for the date (contains comment 101). The user deletes 101 and DELETE returns 204 → exactly **one** subsequent `GET /api/daily-fix/comments?date=…` (spy count 1, no second GET), issued with a cache bypass (`cache: "no-store"` or `"reload"` on the Request, asserted on the recorded init; a cache-busting query alone does not pass); that response (mock: list without 101) is what renders. 101 is absent from the parsed list response (`toStrictEqual` on ids) and from the DOM (`queryByText` of its content null, no row with its id); the stale cached list is never rendered after the 204 (no frame shows 101 after the DELETE resolves, checked with fake timers through settle). 0 client comment-cache purges/invalidations (stays compatible with CW16.2 (b)). Same assertions for a repeat-delete 204.

descriptions.AU27.1: (1.31, spec 1.6.8 §0u.3/§0u.7; token request shape) Mock `/oauth/token`; password and refresh each: exactly 1 request to `${BSI base}/oauth/token` (exact URL string, no `/wp-json`, no query), method POST; header name set exactly `accept`, `user-agent`, `content-type` with `Accept: application/json`, `User-Agent: metfixhome-worker/1.0`, `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`; no `authorization` (no HTTP Basic), `x-api-key`, `cookie`, `x-wp-nonce`, `x-forwarded-for`, `x-real-ip`, `true-client-ip`, `forwarded`, `cf-connecting-ip`, nor any header whose value equals the test client IP. Body form-decoded: key set exactly `{grant_type,username,password,client_id,client_secret}` (password: `grant_type=password`, `username=jane`, `password=PW`) or `{grant_type,refresh_token,client_id,client_secret}` (refresh: `refresh_token=REFRESH1`); `client_id === CID` and `client_secret === SECRET_CANARY` from config even when the browser JSON also sends `client_id:"EVIL"`, `client_secret:"EVIL"`, `scope`, `remoteip`; no `scope`, `recaptcha_token`, `remoteip` key. Upstream 5xx → still exactly 1 token request (0 retries); across every §0u.6 outcome 0 requests to any path containing `/auth/login` or `/auth/web-login`. (1.32, spec 1.6.9 §0v.1) Client credentials only in the body, never Basic and never Basic plus body; no `X-API-Key`; prod URL exactly `https://brokenscience.org/oauth/token`. (1.34, spec 1.6.12 §0w.1/§0w.2) **Google code exchange** too: exactly 1 request, same URL/method/header set and the same forbidden headers; body key set exactly `{grant_type,code,redirect_uri,client_id,client_secret}` with `grant_type=authorization_code`, `redirect_uri=https://metfix.org/api/auth/callback`, `client_id === CID` and `client_secret === SECRET_CANARY` from config even when the callback query adds `client_id=EVIL`, `client_secret=EVIL` or `scope`; no `code_verifier`, `scope`, `username`, `password` key. **Staging:** with the BSI base set to `https://brokenstaging.wpengine.com`, the token, `/me` and revoke URLs are exactly `https://brokenstaging.wpengine.com/oauth/token`, `…/wp-json/bsi/v1/me` and `…/oauth/revoke` (same paths as prod; no other env-dependent path).
descriptions.AU27.2: (1.31, §0u.3; `/me` and no claim trust) After token 200, exactly 1 `GET ${BSI base}/wp-json/bsi/v1/me`, header name set exactly `authorization`, `accept`, `user-agent` (`Authorization: Bearer ACCESS1`; 1.32: **no `x-api-key`**, spec 1.6.9 §0v.1 Q2), no body, no IP header, no `cookie`. Token JSON carries `user_id: 999` and `ACCESS1` is a JWT with `sub: 999`; `/me` returns `id: 7` → the stored session's `bsi_user_id` is exactly `7` (DO record) and `public_name` = `/me.display_name`; nothing reads 999. `can_moderate`: `"true"`, `1`, `"1"`, `{}`, `null`, absent → `/api/auth/me` `moderator: false`; JSON `true` → `true`. On login, `/me` 401, 403, 500, 200 with `id: "7"` (string), 200 without `id`, bad JSON → 503 `{"error":"unavailable"}` (never `invalid_login`), R8b +1, no `Set-Cookie` for `__Host-mfx_sid`, no DO session written, and no later request carries `ACCESS1`. (1.32, §0v.3) On refresh, `/me` 401 → session ended (DO storage empty, KV `/me` entry deleted, the user call 401, `/api/auth/me` `{"signed_in":false}`); `/me` 403/500/string `id`/bad JSON → 503, and the DO holds the new pair `ACCESS2`/R1 (stored in one `put` before `/me`, 1.33 per spec 1.6.11), never R0; identity/`can_moderate` unchanged from the last good `/me`. `avatar_url` never appears in any `/api/auth/*` response.
descriptions.AU27.3: (1.31, §0u.6; error mapping, error-shape uniformity, Retry-After clamp) One case per §0u.6 row, password and refresh: exact status, exact body bytes, exact header set (ignoring `Date`), and R8a/R8b/R8c DO storage before/after equal to the row's counter column. By code, not status: `invalid_grant` at 400 and at 401 → identical 401 `{"error":"invalid_login"}`, R8a +1; `invalid_client` at 400 and at 401, `unauthorized_client`, `unsupported_grant_type`, `invalid_request`, a `bsi_code` halt, unknown code `"nope"`, missing `error` field, the missing-grant 500 → each 503 `{"error":"unavailable"}`, `Retry-After: 60`, R8a +0. Two 429s differing only in `error_description`/message text → byte-identical responses; no `error_description` or upstream text in any body or header. Retry-After on token 429/5xx and `/me` non-200 uses the AU26.10 table exactly (`17`→17, `0`→1, `0000017`→17, `0000000`→1, `600`→600, `601`→600, `99999`→600, 30-digit→600, 400-digit→600; missing, `""`, `-5`, `abc`, `1.5`, `1e30`, `17abc`, HTTP-date → 60). The login `try_again` body is byte-equal to the signup and comment `try_again` bodies. Client: a login 503 or 429 with `Retry-After: 99999` disables sign-in for exactly 600 s (fake timers; 0 login requests before 600 s; enabled at 600 s). Refresh `invalid_grant` → session ended (`/api/auth/me` → `{"signed_in":false}`); refresh `invalid_client`/429/5xx → 503 and the DO record byte-identical before/after. **(1.32, spec 1.6.9 §0v.3 Q7: map on `error` + grant type, never on status)** Each case sent as **both 400 and 401**: password `invalid_grant` → 401 `{"error":"invalid_login"}`, R8a +1, R8b +1 (both statuses identical bytes); refresh `invalid_grant` → session ended (DO `deleteAll`, KV `/me` deleted), the user-acting call 401, `/api/auth/me` `{"signed_in":false}`, exactly 1 token POST (both statuses identical outcome); `invalid_client` (incl. the BSI guard halt `{error:"invalid_client", error_description, bsi_code}`), `unauthorized_client`, `unsupported_grant_type`, `invalid_request` on each grant → 503 `{"error":"unavailable"}`, `Retry-After: 60` (login R8b +1; refresh: DO pair unchanged); `bsi_code` and `error_description` text absent from every response byte. Refresh 200 without `refresh_token` → 503, pair unchanged.
descriptions.AU27.4: (1.31, §0u.5; Worker reCAPTCHA and order) Siteverify on login: exactly 1 POST per login that passes R8b, form body key set exactly `{secret,response}` (`secret=RSECRET`, `response=TOK`, no `remoteip`), action `login`, hostname `metfix.org`, score `0.49` → 403 / `0.5` → proceeds. Call-order spy on an accepted login: config check → R8a → R8b → siteverify → R8c slot-take → `/oauth/token` → `/me`, exactly. Siteverify fail (missing/`""` token, `success:false`, low score, wrong action or hostname) → 403 `try_again`, R8b +1, R8a +0, R8c storage unchanged, 0 `/oauth/token`; siteverify 500/timeout (3 s)/non-JSON → 503 `Retry-After: 60`, R8b +1, R8c unchanged, 0 `/oauth/token`. One IP, 30 logins in 60 s with siteverify pass and token `invalid_grant` → exactly 20 siteverify calls, 20 R8c slots, 20 token calls; 21–30 → 429 `rate_limited` from R8b with 0 siteverify, 0 R8c, 0 token; then a second IP: 5 proceed (R8c 25), its 6th → 429 from R8c with 1 siteverify and 0 token. The 20th request from the first IP reaches siteverify, the 21st doesn't.
descriptions.AU27.5: (1.31, §0u.2 D3; missing config) Each of `BSI_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `METFIX_ORG_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, the BSI base URL and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET`, missing and `""` in turn, for login and for a refresh-triggering user call → 503 `{"error":"unavailable"}`, `Retry-After: 60`; 0 requests on the injected `fetch` (0 siteverify, 0 token, 0 `/me`); 0 `LOGIN_THROTTLE` `idFromName` calls and R8a/R8b/R8c storage unchanged; exactly one log line `auth_config_missing` naming the field, and no line contains any configured value. Static: exactly one `Env` declaration under `worker/**` (non-test), and those four `env.*` fields are read only inside `worker/upstream.ts`.
descriptions.AU27.6: (1.31, §0u.2/§0u.4 SX-1; secret containment, scan + build + runtime) **(a) Scan:** `METFIX_ORG_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` in `worker/**/*.ts` (excl. tests/fixtures) appears only in `worker/upstream.ts` and the single `Env` declaration; 0 hits in `client/**`, `shared/**`, `vite.config.*`, `.env*`, `.dev.vars*`, and `wrangler.jsonc` `vars`; no `VITE_` name containing `OAUTH` or `SECRET` anywhere. **(b) Build:** `npm run build:cf` with `METFIX_ORG_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=<canary>` and `VITE_METFIX_ORG_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=<canary>` in the process env → 0 occurrences of the canary or the binding name in every file under `dist/**` (vacuity: ≥1 file scanned, scan prints the count). **(c) Runtime, canary secret:** across every §0u.6 outcome (password and refresh) plus comment GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE/like, signup, Google sign-in, logout and `/api/auth/me`: the canary appears in exactly one place per token request, the `client_secret` form field of a POST to `${BSI base}/oauth/token`, and in 0 other outbound requests (any URL, header or body, including siteverify, `/me`, comments, signup, revoke and Google); 0 occurrences in any response status text, header or body, including every `Set-Cookie` name and value; 0 in any KV or DO stored value; 0 in captured `console.*` (raw, base64, base64url, URL-encoded, JSON-escaped). Vacuity: the 200 case's token request does contain it. (1.32, §0v.1 Q6) Explicitly: 0 canary in each `POST /oauth/revoke` request (form body keys exactly `token`, `token_type_hint`; no `client_secret`, `client_id`, `X-API-Key`, `Authorization`) and 0 in each `/me` request; the secret's only destination stays the `/oauth/token` body.
descriptions.AU27.7: (1.32 rewrite, spec 1.6.9 §0v.4/§0v.5; refresh rotation) Rotating `/oauth/token` mock (R0 accepted once → `ACCESS2` + R1, then R0 → `invalid_grant`; the mock records every `refresh_token` it receives). (a) After one refresh the DO holds `ACCESS2`/R1 written in exactly one storage `put` of the encrypted pair (R7), and the next refresh sends R1; R0 appears in the mock's record exactly once over the whole test. (b) Refresh `invalid_grant` (status 400, and again with 401) → the user-acting call 401, `/api/auth/me` `{"signed_in":false}`, DO storage empty, KV `/me` entry deleted. (c) Refresh 5xx → 503, DO pair byte-identical to before. (d) 200 without `refresh_token` → 503, DO pair byte-identical to before. (e) (1.33, spec 1.6.11) Token 200 with R1, then `/me` 500 → that call 503, DO holds R1 (not R0), the next refresh sends R1, R0 appears exactly once in the mock log. (f) (1.33) Token 200 with R1, then `/me` 401 → that call 401, `/api/auth/me` `{"signed_in":false}`, DO storage empty. Stricter failure coverage for (e)/(f) is in AU27.9. Exactly 1 `/me` call per successful refresh; `bsi_user_id`/`public_name` follow it. (1.34, spec 1.6.12 §0w.1) Cases (a)–(f) run twice, once with a password-created session and once with a Google-created session (AU27.10 (a)). descriptions.AU27.8: (QA ID 1.32, Web Lead request; spec §0v.4 single-flight) Rotating mock, one session: 20 concurrent user-acting calls (comment POST, leaderboard GET, like) needing refresh, across two isolates → exactly **1** `/oauth/token` POST and exactly 1 `/me` GET; all 20 succeed with `Bearer ACCESS2`; R0 sent exactly once. Failure shared: same setup with the mock answering `invalid_grant` → exactly 1 token POST, all 20 get 401, DO empty. Same setup with mock 503 → exactly 1 token POST, all 20 get 503, DO pair unchanged. A second token POST in any variant fails the row.
descriptions.AU27.9: (QA ID 1.32; 1.33 aligned to Web Lead ruling, spec 1.6.11 §0v.4; strict superset of AU27.7 (e)/(f)) Rotating mock: token 200 returns `ACCESS2`/R1 (R0 now dead). **Store order:** the DO pair `ACCESS2`/R1 is written in exactly one `put` **before** the `/me` request goes out (the test reads DO storage from inside the `/me` mock handler and sees R1, not R0). Then `/me` fails, each its own case: 500, 403, timeout, network throw, bad JSON, 200 with string `id`, 200 without `id` → that request 503 `{"error":"unavailable"}` with `Retry-After`; DO holds `ACCESS2`/R1 (byte check of the decrypted pair; refresh token ≠ R0); the next user-acting call sends R1 (or uses `ACCESS2` if unexpired), never R0. `/me` 401 → that request 401, DO storage empty, KV `/me` deleted, `/api/auth/me` `{"signed_in":false}`, 0 further token POSTs over 3 later calls. Every case: R0 appears **exactly once** in the mock's log for the whole test and is never the stored refresh token at any later read.
descriptions.AU27.Q1: (QA ID 1.32 as AU27.10, renamed 1.34 for the spec ID collision; Web Lead request; no retry loop) Refresh `invalid_grant` (400 and 401, each its own case) → exactly 1 token POST; then 5 further user-acting calls with the same cookie → each 401 `signed_out` with **0** upstream requests (0 token, 0 `/me`, 0 BSI) and no alarm set (`storage.getAlarm()` null); total token POSTs stay 1; DO storage empty, KV `/me` deleted; `/api/auth/me` `{"signed_in":false}`.
descriptions.AU27.10: (spec 1.6.12 §0w.1/§0w.5; Google code exchange; QA-tightened) Mock `/oauth/token`, `/me` and a recorder on every outbound request. Callback reached through the in-Worker bridge with `code=CODE` and a valid state. **(a) Success:** exactly 1 POST to `${BSI base}/oauth/token` (exact URL; prod `https://brokenscience.org/oauth/token`, staging `https://brokenstaging.wpengine.com/oauth/token`), header set as AU27.1, form body `toStrictEqual({grant_type:"authorization_code",code:CODE,redirect_uri:"https://metfix.org/api/auth/callback",client_id:CID,client_secret:SECRET_CANARY})`. Then exactly 1 `/me` GET with `Bearer ACCESS1` and the AU27.2 header set. Session cookie set and DO pair `ACCESS1`/R0 written only after `/me` 200. **0 requests to any URL containing `/wp-json/metfix/v1/proxy/`** (any method; this covers the BSI-C3 `oauth/token` leg) and 0 `x-api-key` headers on any request. No token or secret byte appears in the browser response. `/me` 401 and `/me` 500, each its own case → 503 `unavailable`, no `Set-Cookie`, no DO write. **(b) Errors (code + grant mapping):** code-exchange `invalid_grant` as 400 and as 401 → 401 `{"error":"invalid_login"}`, byte-identical (body and headers apart from `Date`) to the password-grant `invalid_grant` response, R8b +1, no session, 0 `/me`. `invalid_client` (incl. the guard halt with `bsi_code`) → 503, `Retry-After: 60`, `bsi_code` and `error_description` absent from the response. 429 → 503 with the AU26.10 clamp. Missing `BSI_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` or `METFIX_ORG_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` → 503 with 0 outbound requests and no limiter slot used. Every case: exactly 1 token POST (0 retries). **(c) Google refresh:** for the session from (a), the rotating mock (R0 → `ACCESS2`/R1, then R0 dead) gives exactly 1 POST with body `toStrictEqual({grant_type:"refresh_token",refresh_token:R0,client_id:CID,client_secret:SECRET_CANARY})`. The DO already holds R1 when the `/me` mock handler runs (in-handler read, as AU27.9). The next refresh sends R1. R0 appears exactly once in the log. 0 proxy requests.
